related_questions.question: Is money withdrawn from life insurance taxable?

text_blocks.snippet: Generally, withdrawals from cash value life insurance policies are not taxed up to the total premiums paid into the policy (your basis). However, any withdrawals exceeding your basis, which typically represents gains, can be taxed as ordinary income, according to Aflac.

list.snippet: You can generally withdraw up to the amount of premiums you've paid into the policy without incurring taxes.
This is because the premiums you pay are considered your "basis" in the policy.
Any withdrawals up to your basis are not taxed, says Henssler Financial.
If you withdraw more than your basis (the amount you've paid in premiums), the excess amount may be taxed as ordinary income, according to Aflac.
For example, if you've paid $12,000 in premiums and withdraw $15,000, the $3,000 excess would be taxed.

list.title: Modified Endowment Contracts (MECs):
list.snippet: If your policy is classified as a MEC, withdrawals may be taxed differently, potentially with a 10% penalty if you're under 59 1/2.

list.title: Policy Loans:
list.snippet: Loans taken against the cash value are generally not taxed as long as the policy remains in effect and the loan doesn't exceed your basis, according to Transamerica.

list.title: Surrendering a Policy:
list.snippet: If you surrender the policy, any amount exceeding your basis will be taxed.

list.title: Beneficiary Payouts:
list.snippet: Life insurance proceeds paid to a beneficiary are generally not taxable as income, with some exceptions for structured settlements or if the policy was transferred for value.

It's always a good idea to consult with a financial advisor or tax professional for personalized advice regarding your specific life insurance policy and its tax implications, advises Western & Southern.
